Senate passes stopgap funding bill hours before shutdown deadline

By Jane Reporter · November 22, 2026

WASHINGTON — The Senate voted 60 to 38 late Friday to pass a stopgap measure that funds the federal government through January 30, sending the bill to the president hours before a midnight deadline that would have triggered a partial shutdown.

The measure, approved by the House on Thursday, keeps spending at current levels and includes $12 billion in disaster aid for states hit by this autumn's hurricanes. Eleven Republicans joined all but two Democrats in support.

"This is not the bill any of us would have written, but it keeps the lights on," Senate Majority Leader John Doe said on the floor before the vote. "Shutting down the government during the holidays would have hurt millions of families."

Opponents argued that the bill does nothing to address the deficit. Senator Mary Roe called it "another kick of the can that adds to a debt our children will pay," and said she would push for spending caps in the January negotiations.

The White House said in a statement that the president would sign the bill on Saturday. The Office of Management and Budget had begun notifying agencies on Thursday to prepare for a possible lapse in funding.

Lawmakers now face a January 30 deadline to agree on full-year appropriations, with disputes over border security funding and defense spending still unresolved.
